examples.japanese: {大切|たいせつ}な{物|もの}を{忘|わす}れた。
{甘|あま}い{物|もの}が{食|た}べたい。
examples.english: I want to eat something sweet.

examples.japanese: {飲|の}み{物|もの}は{何|なに}がいいですか。
examples.english: What would you like to drink?

examples.japanese: {重|おも}い{物|もの}を{持|も}たないでください。
{人生|じんせい}というのは{難|むずか}しい{物|もの}だ。
{時間|じかん}は{大切|たいせつ}な{物|もの}です。
{愛|あい}とは{不思議|ふしぎ}な{物|もの}だ。
{経験|けいけん}は{貴重|きちょう}な{物|もの}です。
{世|よ}の{中|なか}には{分|わ}からない{物|もの}がたくさんある。
examples.english: There are many things in the world that we don't understand.

notes:
{物|もの} is one of the most versatile words in Japanese, referring to physical objects, abstract things, or general matters. As a noun it typically refers to tangible items, but in combination with adjectives (e.g. {甘|あま}い{物|もの}) it means "something [adjective]."

もの VS こと:
- {物|もの}: concrete or tangible things, or abstract things treated as entities
- こと: abstract matters, facts, events, or actions
- Example: {大切|たいせつ}な{物|もの} (a precious thing/item) vs {大切|たいせつ}なこと (an important matter/fact)

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
- {食|た}べ{物|もの}: food
- {飲|の}み{物|もの}: drink
- {買|か}い{物|もの}: shopping
- {着物|きもの}: kimono, clothes
- {物語|ものがたり}: story, tale
- {荷物|にもつ}: luggage, baggage

GRAMMAR NOTE:
もの (or もん in casual speech) also appears as a sentence-ending particle expressing explanation, reason, or mild complaint: {だって|だって}{高|たか}いんだもの (But it's expensive!).
